answer: A defense uses beacon-scheduled rendezvous sessions. Each epoch, a random beacon sets unpredictable meeting times, and each identity must answer a challenge in a narrow window to keep earnings. An operator with many clones cannot attend overlapping sessions with one signing setup, so duplicates miss slots and fall to zero weight, while honest agents stay available. Attackers must fund separate, always-online infrastructure per identity, eroding sybil profit. Imagine a garden where a zephyr of randomness scatters the schedule, exposing each onyx-dark clone when times collide.
